questions.q: What is a "business domain" in Microsoft Purview?
options: A named, owned boundary that groups data products, glossary terms, OKRs, and critical data elements
A DNS zone used for scan authentication
A single Power BI workspace
A synonym for an Azure subscription
questions.explain: A business domain is a boundary — name, description, owner — that groups the four business concepts: data products, glossary terms, OKRs, and critical data elements.

questions.q: Per the lesson, what does current Purview documentation increasingly call this same feature?
options: A collection
A governance domain
A classification rule set
A scan rule set
questions.explain: Microsoft renamed the feature as Unified Catalog matured — "governance domain" is the newer label for the same "business domain" feature, same five types and rules.

questions.q: What does a domain's "type" (Functional unit, Line of business, Data domain, Regulatory, Project) actually control?
options: Which users can view the domain at all
The maximum number of glossary terms the domain can hold
Nothing behavioral — it's a purely descriptive label explaining why the boundary exists
Whether the domain can have a parent domain
questions.explain: Domain type is descriptive only — a Regulatory domain and a Functional unit domain behave identically under the hood.

questions.q: How deep can business domains nest, and how many can a tenant hold, per the lesson?
options: Unlimited depth, unlimited count
Two levels deep, 50 domains maximum
Up to five levels deep, up to 200 domains
Domains cannot nest at all
questions.explain: Domains can nest up to five levels deep, and a tenant can hold as many as 200 domains total — deliberately bounded to stay a readable hierarchy.

questions.q: What has to happen before a glossary term or data product inside a domain can be published?
options: The domain itself has to be published first
The term must first be scanned by an automated classifier
Nothing — concepts publish independently of their domain's status
The domain must be deleted and recreated
questions.explain: A domain sits in draft, invisible to others, until its owner publishes it — and a domain has to be published before any business concept inside it can be published either.
